Vi söker dig som är leg sjuksköterska eller fysioterapeut och har relevant klinisk arbetslivserfarenhet. Vi söker dig som är intresserad av den svenska affärens potential och dess marknad. Du bygger goda och långsiktiga relationer. Du greppar konceptuella uppdrag och hanterar komplexa diskussioner. Din nyfikenhet gör att du ställer frågor och du har fallenhet för presentation och "story telling". Du är kund- och målorienterad. Noggrann med detaljer mot kund och påläst i beslutsfattande situationer. Du är en självständig och kommunikativ person, som trivs med att arbeta i team och har företagets vision i fokus. Meriterande är om du har erfarenhet av Medtech och kännedom om att arbeta med LOU.

Företaget - Care of Sweden har en konkret vision - att tillsammans med vårdgivare eliminera trycksår - och är stolta över att våra produkter kan vara med och göra skillnad för vårdtagare varje dag. Vi återfinns inom det segment av medicintekniska produkter som används som hjälpmedel för att förebygga och behandla trycksår; däribland madrasser, sittdynor och positioneringskuddar. Vi är stolta över att ägna våra dagar åt att minska onödigt lidande. Vårt löfte är att ge vården goda förutsättningar för en individanpassad vård och en god hälsoekonomi. Vi kallar det löftet för Supporting Life.

Kunskap, glädje och omtanke - För att göra vår kultur enkel att sprida och ta till sig, sammanfattar vi den i tre kärnvärden. Tre ord som är viktiga för oss och som genomsyrar allt vi tar oss för. Tre enkla ord, omsorgsfullt valda och fyllda med mening. De är viktiga var för sig men det är tillsammans som de beskriver oss bäst - en kombination av stora hjärtan och skarpa sinnen.

Ansvarsområde:

  • CAS skall ta ansvar för den försäljning som sker på respektive avtal i tilldelat distrikt under framför allt avropsfasen.
  • CAS arbetar proaktivt under avropsperioden för att bygga relationer med nyckelpersoner så som vårdutvecklare, patientsäkerhetsenheter, MAS, MAR, hjälpmedelskonsulenter och andra beslutsfattare med framförallt klinisk karaktär.
  • Aktivt bidra till företagets vision och framtida tillväxt genom nära samarbete med Contract Manager på tilldelat distrikt.
  • Delta i och leda förbättrings- och målarbete som rör verksamhetsområdet.
  • Bygga relationer med avropande kunder och fungera konsultativt.
  • Att få företagets avtalskunder att lyckas med sitt trycksårsarbete på avtalade produkter.

Arbetsuppgifter:

  • Aktiv och regelbunden kundbearbetning på befintliga kunder.
  • Sälja in det helhetskoncept Care of Sweden erbjuder genom klinisk kunskap och de koncept som företaget har.
  • Aktivt bidra till att företagets avtalskunder förbättrar sina kunskaper och rutiner kring trycksårsförebyggande arbete, madrasser och positionering för att minska patienters lidande och förbättra hälsoekonomin.
  • Genomföra utbildningar av klinisk karaktär samt produkt. CAS ska verka proaktivt för att genomföra större utbildningsinsatser istället för många små.
  • Planering, dokumentation och administration.
  • Följa säljprocessen och säkerställa användandet av företagets produkter.
  • Upprätthålla god produkt-, kund- och konkurrentkännedom samt förmedla denna i bolaget.
  • Att sköta sina åtaganden i företagets CRM & Verksamhetssystem.
  • Delta på mässor, konferenser och föreläsningar kopplat till trycksår, produkter, medicinteknik el liknande relevanta forum kopplat till produkt och vision.
  • Samverka med Marknadsavdelning för att skapa utskick, bidra till relevant information i nyhetsbrev och marknadsmaterial.
  • Att aktivt uppdatera kunskaper kring forskning, studier och nyheter inom det kliniska området.
  • Genomföra hearings el dyl inför upphandlingar.

jobs.description:
KLDiscovery, a leading global provider of electronic discovery, information governance and data recovery services, is currently seeking a Software Engineer II, the position will assist in review and analysis of applications, product development, and enhancements including documentation, code development, and unit testing of releases while adhering to KLDiscovery development processes and workflows with supervision and direction from lead developers and superiors.

Responsibilities

  • Create and maintain software to monitor, maintain, and administrate systems
  • Develop automated solutions for systems upgrades across a variety of platforms
  • Test, refine, and document software · Support bug fixes and implement enhancements to applications in Production
  • Develop automated test suites, including unit tests, functional tests, and regression tests
  • Create design and user documentation as needed
  • Utilize, communicate and enforce coding standards Seek and participate in personal development opportunities to maintain a detailed knowledge of industry standards, engineering best practices, and business needs
  • Provide Technical Support - bug fixes and implement enhancements to applications in Production within defined SLA

  • Work in a team or with multiple organizational departments in a dynamic and rapidly changing environment · Adhere to development processes and workflows.

Qualifications

  • 3+ years of experience in .NET/C# and front-end experience- Angular preferred
  • Good knowledge in unit/integration testing
  • SQL databases, preferably MS SQL and PostgreSQL
  • Analytical and problem-solving skills, Focus on continuous improvement
  • Excellent communication skills, Being a team player

  • Fluent English communication skills (C1 level or equivalent).

Who We Are

KLDiscovery provides technology-enabled services and software to help law firms, corporations, government agencies and consumers solve complex data challenges. The company, with offices in 26 locations across 17 countries, is a global leader in delivering best-in-class eDiscovery, information governance and data recovery solutions to support the litigation, regulatory compliance, internal investigation and data recovery and management needs of our clients.

Serving clients for over 30 years, KLDiscovery offers data collection and forensic investigation, early case assessment, electronic discovery and data processing, application software and data hosting for web-based document reviews, and managed document review services. In addition, through its global Ontrack Data Recovery business, KLDiscovery delivers world-class data recovery, email extraction and restoration, data destruction and tape management.

KLDiscovery is an Equal Opportunity Employer.

Job Description Summary:

The Raymond A. Mason School of Business at William & Mary is recruiting a pool of Adjunct Faculty (Section Leads) to lead one or more 7.5-week asynchronous course sections within the Online MBA program. Please visit the following website to learn more about these programs:

Section Leads serve a vital role within our online programs and are valued members of the Raymond A. Mason School of Business (MSOB) and the William & Mary community. Under the supervision of the Faculty Lead, Section Leads facilitate their assigned course section(s) by posting course announcements, engaging in discussion boards, offering weekly office hours, responding to student inquiries, monitoring student progress, grading student assignments, and providing students with substantive, timely feedback. Section Leads are provided with professional learning opportunities and are invited to attend on-campus events.

Job Description:

Position duties include:

  • Maintain frequent and open communication with William & Mary faculty and staff through email, mail, telephone, and any other medium deemed appropriate.
  • Complete online instructor orientation and technology training before teaching online for the Mason School and complete continuing training each year after.
  • Review course syllabus, content, activities, and assignments prior to the term start date.
  • Adhere to the course design, instructional and grading guidelines, and due dates.
  • Post a minimum of two weekly announcements relevant to the course content and learning activities.
  • Respond to student inquiries within 24 hours.
  • Provide students with timely, personalized, and substantive feedback on graded assignment submissions.
  • Grade assignments and exams in a timely manner based on the instructions/rubrics provided by the Faculty Lead (48 – 72 hours).
  • Monitor and participate in weekly discussion boards.
  • Offer virtual office hours (drop-in or by appointment) totaling at least one hour per week for individual or group consultation and communicate this information through announcements and the course calendar.
  • Monitor student progress and notify the Faculty Lead when a student is unresponsive or at risk of failing.
  • Meet weekly with the Faculty Lead during regularly scheduled calls throughout the course.
  • Submit final grades to the Faculty Lead according to William & Mary and Mason School grading policies and the Online Programs calendar.
  • Submit Section Lead end-of-semester reflection form and attend debriefing meetings as applicable.
  • Section Leads typically spend 15 to 20 hours per week on the duties listed above.

Required Qualifications: Please make sure your cover letter and resume clearly indicate how you meet the following required qualifications:

  • Master's Degree directly related to discipline
  • Master's Degree directly related to the discipline OR a Bachelor's Degree with extensive and significant experience related to the discipline.
  • Experience providing instruction to adult learners in an academic or corporate setting.
  • Demonstrated excellence in communicating and collaborating in digital environments.
  • Demonstrated commitment to creating an inclusive and supportive learning environment for a diverse student population.
  • Demonstrated commitment to upholding William & Mary’s historic reputation for academic excellence and innovation.

Preferred Qualifications: Please make sure your cover letter and resume clearly indicate whether you meet any of the preferred qualifications:

  • Ph.D. or other doctoral degree directly related to the discipline.
  • Demonstrated excellence in teaching adult learners in a professional degree program.
  • Experience providing online instruction.
  • Enthusiasm for delivering education in an online mode.
  • Proficiency using video conferencing technologies and web-based collaboration platforms.
  • Experience using Canvas or a similar learning management system.

Other details: For full consideration, please upload a Resume, Cover Letter, Teaching Statement, and Unofficial Transcripts reflecting a degree associated with the subject area being taught.

  • The review of applications is ongoing, and only those selected for an interview will be contacted.
  • Hired candidates are required to provide official transcripts prior to the contracted start date.
  • This part-time position is restricted to the term in which it is assigned and hired and is not eligible for benefits.
  • This position is not eligible for work visa sponsorship.

jobs.excerpt: Solution Enginner/ Sales Consultant Our Company Elsevier is a global information analytics company that helps institutions and professionals progress science, advance healthcare and improve performance for the benefit of humanity.
jobs.description:
Solution Enginner/ Sales Consultant


Our Company

Elsevier is a global information analytics company that helps institutions and professionals progress science, advance healthcare and improve performance for the benefit of humanity. We serve the research, academic and clinical communities through the application of technology and analytics to content. In this way, we empower those communities to contribute to social progress, to enhance human well-being and to share and expand the breadth of human knowledge.


Purpose of the Job

Solutions Engineers work with Account Managers - Solutions to grow sales opportunities within a region and/or market and take them to close. They focus on understanding, documenting and validating with the clients what are the customer’s needs and success criteria and how Elsevier can help to achieve them. They leverage a deep domain expertise and in-depth technical skillset to explain the benefits of Elsevier’s Academic Information Systems portfolio (and the wider Research Intelligence portfolio) to potential clients through demonstrations and sales presentations, then set milestones for testing during pre-sales and validating customer feedback.


  • Pre-sale: Prepares persona-tailored in-depth presentations and technical demos, informed by their in-depth needs analysis with the customer. Engages with Product/Marketing to ensure understanding of latest features and product roadmaps to be leveraged during sales conversations.
  • Sales: Review opportunity and account information in CRM to meet with Account Manager - Solutions and prepare for demo/technical discussion. Conduct demo and log all project requirements and customer needs in CRM.
  • Post-sales: Gathers insights from customer, Customer Success and Account Manager – Solutions on demo and value story and engages with Implementation Manager to ensure successful hand-off.

Key Result Areas / Primary Accountabilities


  • Drive technical sales process - Meeting with clients to discuss their software solution needs. Conducting detailed client discovery focused on the customer needs analysis & solution development in alignment with the Account Managers. Effectively communicating the value proposition to clients.
  • Support Account Manager- Drafting and delivering presentations with in-depth information on targeted software products, reflecting an in-depth understanding of client needs and how Elsevier solutions can fit in. Supporting the Account Manager with all technical related queries. Supporting User Group meetings, conferences, working closely with Marketing team on formulation of use cases, value proposition & client endorsement.
  • Drive tender process - Understanding of tender requirements, lead technical tender requirements and responses, close cooperation with tender team on tender write-ups.
  • Design solution and overall proposal to meet client needs and realize success & satisfaction - Perform the more technical parts of the sales process and design to the client’s needs and promised functionality of the solution, thereby achieving a high customer satisfaction based on client success metrics. Contribute to Product roadmap discussion and strategy; strategizing with the Sales & Product team to create feasible software solutions.
  • Provide support during implementation and post-installation – Ensure translation of client needs via handover to the implementation team & customer success manager; support the Implementation Manager and Customer Success Manager as needed in delivering a successful implementation.
  • Play an active role in generating referrals and reference customers – As a trusted partner during the pre-sales and handover process, aiming to have highly satisfied clients who generate referrals and become active reference customers. Support the finding of new potential clients through their network.

Qualifications – (education, competencies, skills, experience)


  • Bachelor’s degree in computer science, Software Engineering or Management Information Systems or similar field
  • 5+ years of sales experience as a Solution Engineer/Pre-Sales Consultant or similar
  • SaaS / Software as a Service experience is a plus.
  • Publishing expertise, experience with publishing systems and workflows is a plus.
  • Ability to present ideas in a clean, user-friendly way.
  • Great communication skills
  • Exceptional relationship building skills.
  • Experienced in working in an international matrixed organisation is a plus.
  • Fluent in English
  • Extensive experience with selling, servicing, implementing software systems.
  • Proven experience in complex solution-sales approach - “consultative selling”
  • Excellent analytical skills, attention to detail
  • Excellent software demonstration and presentation skills
  • Ability to create big-picture software solutions.

Job Description Summary:

The Raymond A. Mason School of Business at William & Mary is recruiting a pool of Adjunct Faculty (Section Leads) to lead one or more 7.5-week asynchronous course sections within the Online Master of Science in Business Analytics and Online MBA programs. Please visit the following website to learn more about these program:

Leads serve a vital role within our online programs and are valued members of the Raymond A. Mason School of Business (MSOB) and the William & Mary community. Under the supervision of the Faculty Lead, Section Leads facilitate their assigned course section(s) by posting course announcements, engaging in discussion boards, offering weekly office hours, responding to student inquiries, monitoring student progress, grading student assignments, and providing students with substantive, timely feedback. Section Leads are provided with professional learning opportunities and are invited to attend on-campus events.

Job Description:

Position duties include:

  • Maintain frequent and open communication with William & Mary faculty and staff through email, mail, telephone, and any other medium deemed appropriate.
  • Complete online instructor orientation and technology training before teaching online for the Mason School and complete continuing training each year after.
  • Review course syllabus, content, activities, and assignments prior to the term start date.
  • Adhere to the course design, instructional and grading guidelines, and due dates.
  • Post a minimum of two weekly announcements relevant to the course content and learning activities.
  • Respond to student inquiries within 24 hours.
  • Provide students with timely, personalized, and substantive feedback on graded assignment submissions.
  • Grade assignments and exams in a timely manner based on the instructions/rubrics provided by the Faculty Lead (48 – 72 hours).
  • Monitor and participate in weekly discussion boards.
  • Offer virtual office hours (drop-in or by appointment) totaling at least one hour per week for individual or group consultation and communicate this information through announcements and the course calendar.
  • Monitor student progress and notify the Faculty Lead when a student is unresponsive or at risk of failing.
  • Meet weekly with the Faculty Lead during regularly scheduled calls throughout the course.
  • Submit final grades to the Faculty Lead according to William & Mary and Mason School grading policies and the Online Programs calendar.
  • Submit Section Lead end-of-semester reflection form and attend debriefing meetings as applicable.
  • Section Leads typically spend 15 to 20 hours per week on the duties listed above.

Required Qualifications: Please make sure your cover letter and resume clearly indicate how you meet the following required qualifications:

  • Master’s degree in business/data analytics, computer science, industrial engineering, information systems, information technology, operations management, operations research, or a closely related field.
  • Significant expertise and relevant professional and/or instructional experience in business/data analytics, computer science, industrial engineering, information systems, information technology, operations management, operations research, or a closely related field.
  • Experience providing instruction to adult learners in an academic or corporate setting.
  • Demonstrated excellence in communicating and collaborating in digital environments.
  • Demonstrated commitment to creating an inclusive and supportive learning environment for a diverse student population.
  • Demonstrated commitment to upholding William & Mary’s historic reputation for academic excellence and innovation.

Preferred Qualifications: Please make sure your cover letter and resume clearly indicate whether you meet any of the preferred qualifications:

  • Doctoral degree directly related to the discipline.
  • Demonstrated excellence teaching adult learners in a professional degree program.
  • Experience providing online instruction.
  • Enthusiasm for delivering education in an online mode.
  • Proficiency using video conferencing technologies and web-based collaboration platforms.
  • Experience using Canvas or a similar learning management system.

Other details:

  • For full consideration, please upload a Resume, Cover Letter, Teaching Statement, and Unofficial Transcripts reflecting a degree associated with the subject area being taught.
  • The review of applications is ongoing, and only those selected for an interview will be contacted.
  • Hired candidates are required to provide official transcripts prior to the contracted start date.
  • This part-time position is restricted to the term in which it is assigned and hired and is not eligible for benefits.
  • This position is not eligible for work visa sponsorship.

jobs.excerpt: Turn interest into bookings—and keep players coming backCommunity Sports Partners operates sports and recreation businesses.
jobs.description:
Turn interest into bookings—and keep players coming back

Community Sports Partners operates sports and recreation businesses. We are looking for someone who combines strong email and SMS marketing skills with sales follow-through and organized day-to-day coordination.

Your work will connect three things: campaigns that generate interest, conversations that turn interest into bookings, and pickup games that run smoothly enough for people to return. You will help sell available sports facility time and permit-backed bookings, support pickup-game operations remotely, and build email and SMS campaigns that increase participation and repeat business.

What you will own

Email and SMS marketing

• Plan, write, build and send campaigns promoting available facility time, pickup games, registration opportunities and relevant offers.

• Create useful segments by location, sport, expressed interest, booking history and engagement.

• Build and improve welcome messages, lead follow-up, incomplete-booking recovery where supported, reminders, repeat-booking and win-back flows.

• Write clear English copy with specific offers and calls to action. Adapt existing brand assets into mobile-friendly emails.

• Check audiences, dates, time zones, prices, links, personalization and suppression rules before launch.

• Monitor delivery failures, bounces, complaints and opt-outs; maintain consent records and healthy lists.

• Test messaging, timing, offers and journeys, then report qualified enquiries, paid bookings, repeat participation and revenue alongside engagement metrics.

Permit and facility-time sales

• Maintain an accurate view of available locations, dates, time slots, capacity and approved pricing.

• Respond to enquiries from teams, coaches, leagues, organizers and other customers looking for sports space.

• Understand what customers need, recommend suitable availability, prepare approved quotes and follow up through booking and payment confirmation.

• Keep the sales pipeline current, document customer commitments and pursue renewals or repeat bookings.

• Coordinate with the operations team before promising availability or exceptions. Escalate pricing, terms and conflicts outside your authority.

Pickup-game coordination

• Create and maintain accurate game listings, including location, start time, capacity, pricing and player instructions.

• Monitor registrations and fill levels; use targeted outreach to help fill available places.

• Coordinate with local hosts and venue contacts, making sure each game has the information and support it needs.

• Manage routine player questions and waitlists, and communicate approved changes promptly.

• Identify low-enrolment games, host gaps or venue problems early and escalate cancellation, refund or safety decisions to the appropriate manager.

• Track attendance, feedback and repeat participation, and use what you learn to improve future games.

This is one role advertised across multiple recruitment locations. Applicants throughout Latin America are welcome. Please apply once using your preferred location listing.

Requirements

What we are looking for

• Practical experience building email campaigns and automations, plus hands-on SMS experience.

• Strong written and spoken English for North American customer conversations.

• Confidence following up with leads, explaining an offer and asking for the booking.

• Strong attention to detail with schedules, prices, customer records and competing deadlines.

• Experience with a CRM and an email/SMS platform; examples include Klaviyo, ActiveCampaign, HubSpot, Mailchimp or comparable tools. Experience with every platform is not required.

• Comfort using spreadsheets and reports to understand conversion, bookings and campaign performance.

• Dependable communication and willingness to own the next action until an issue is resolved.

• Availability to work evenings and weekends in Toronto/Eastern time is required. This is when most games and customer activity take place, so these shifts are a core part of the role. The specific weekly schedule will be agreed before hiring.

Experience in sports, venue bookings, inside sales, event coordination, customer service or ecommerce retention is helpful. You should enjoy both campaign execution and customer follow-through.

What success looks like

In the first month, learn the inventory, customer journeys and operating processes; audit existing campaigns and establish a reliable follow-up and QA routine.

Over the following two months, take ownership of the campaign calendar and sales pipeline, improve priority automations, and make pickup-game coordination dependable. We will agree measurable goals for paid bookings, use of available facility time, game fill rates, repeat participation and service quality after reviewing the baseline.

Apply with your resume and answer the questions in this application. Remove customer data and confidential employer information from examples. Applicants throughout Latin America are welcome; the selected location is a recruitment location, not a residence requirement.

Required assessments

Please complete both standard assessments before or shortly after applying, using the same email address as your application. If you have already completed them for Community Sports Partners with that email, indicate this in the application.

  • Culture Index survey
  • Criteria GAME assessment — English

Benefits

Remote from Latin America. Monthly base of US$800–US$1,000 based on experience, plus expected variable commissions of US$500–US$1,000. Expected total US$1,300–US$2,000 per month. Commissions depend on performance and are not guaranteed. Evening and weekend work in Toronto/Eastern time is required, when most games and customer activity take place. The specific weekly schedule and commission terms will be agreed before hiring.

jobs.title: Project Manager (IT) - Senior JP1045
jobs.excerpt: Project Name: Artificial Intelligence Delivery and Enablement Scope: AI Delivery & Enablement (AIDE) leads the Government of Alberta's adoption, delivery, and responsible use of artificial intelligence to enhance productivity, improve decision-making, and support better outcomes for Albertans.
jobs.description:
Project Name:

Artificial Intelligence Delivery and Enablement

Scope:

AI Delivery & Enablement (AIDE) leads the Government of Alberta's adoption, delivery, and responsible use of artificial intelligence to enhance productivity, improve decision-making, and support better outcomes for Albertans. AIDE's approach rests on three mutually reinforcing pillars: capability building through the Alberta AI Academy; governed enterprise AI tools deployed under a unified access, training, and compliance model; and an operational delivery model that supports both new AI application builds and sustainment of live AI services.

The resources will report to the AIDE Executive Director and will be assigned to directors as priorities require. They will lead and support AI enablement projects across the branch, including:

  • rolling out and managing enterprise AI licences, consumption and cost recovery across ministries
  • delivering the AI cloud platform, integration and access work that AI tools depend on
  • aligning projects with governance, security, privacy and intake requirements
  • supporting training, adoption and change management with ministry champions

They will also take pilots through to governed enterprise service. Current demand exceeds branch capacity, and these resources are needed to avoid delayed adoption and to continue successfully enabling our services and delivery obligations.

Work Streams:

This role spans four connected work streams. Each Project Manager may lead projects in one or more of them, depending on branch priorities.

Enterprise AI licence and consumption enablement. Planning and delivering the rollout, allocation and lifecycle management of enterprise AI licences across the department and the broader GoA. This includes Microsoft 365 Copilot, Copilot Studio, Microsoft 365 Copilot Cowork, Google Gemini Enterprise (including Gemini Notebook) and Claude Enterprise, as well as additional providers, models and agents added to the approved catalogue. The work covers:

ministry allocation models and quota management

ServiceNow request and provisioning workflows

chargeback and cost-recovery mechanisms

reassignment and reclamation of underused licences

reporting on utilization, consumption and spend that supports adoption targets and cost transparency

AI cloud platform and integration. Planning and delivering the platform and integration work that enterprise AI depends on. This includes Microsoft 365 and Azure tenant services, Google Cloud landing zones and project provisioning, sandbox and lab environments, on-premises and hybrid service integration, and direct-to-provider AI model access and API enablement. The work covers:

identity and access configuration

data connector and grounding-source enablement

integration of AI services into existing business systems

monitoring of AI services and agents

model lifecycle and deprecation migrations

transition of new capabilities into ongoing operations

Governance, security, privacy and intake alignment. Ensuring every project moves through the branch's intake, assessment and approval pathway and meets GoA requirements before a capability is released to users. The work covers:

  • coordinating Security Threat and Risk Assessments (STRAs) and Privacy Impact Assessments (PIAs)
  • aligning with information-classification and data-residency requirements
  • applying the branch's responsible AI standards and guardrails
  • working with privacy, security, legal, enterprise architecture and procurement partners to obtain the approvals each project needs

Training, adoption and change management. Planning the people side of each rollout so that capabilities are used safely and effectively once enabled. The work covers:

  • coordinating with the Alberta AI Academy on role-based training and learning pathways
  • working through the AI Delivery and Enablement Champion network and ministry leadership on adoption planning and use-case identification
  • developing user guidance, communications and support pathways
  • tracking training completion and adoption against targets

A recurring pattern across all four streams is moving capabilities from evaluation to governed enterprise service. This means taking an assessed request through intake and standing up a time-boxed pilot with a defined user cohort. It then means collecting use cases and feedback, and confirming that the platform is ready and that security and privacy approvals are in place. Cost, licensing and catalogue treatment are determined, and the end-to-end request, training and support experience is established. The pilot closes with a recommendation on enterprise enablement and handoff to operations.

The Project Manager will review and understand departmental and corporate policies, business rules, data requirements, information management and security classification obligations, responsible AI standards, and supporting system processes. They will ensure project objectives and schedules align with GoA and branch priorities. Resources report to the AIDE Executive Director and may support several directors and sponsors at once, so they must manage shifting priorities and dependencies across projects. The resource will provide recommendations, including resource requirements, dependencies, interdependencies, policy implications pertaining to internal and external influences, and the methodology to be applied.

This resource will have working knowledge and experience of enterprise IT and cloud environments. This includes Microsoft 365, Azure and Google Cloud services, SaaS licensing and tenant administration concepts, cloud subscription and consumption models, identity and access management, and a general understanding of line-of-business applications and architectures. Familiarity with generative AI and agentic AI concepts is required, such as assistants, agents, grounding, model selection, responsible AI risks, and token- or consumption-based cost drivers. The resource must have a sound understanding of:

  • IT change and communication management

User Acceptance Testing frameworks

security and privacy assessment processes (STRA and PIA)

They must also have experience delivering change into large, federated organizations where adoption depends on distributed business champions rather than direct authority.

Excellent written and verbal communication skills are essential, including the ability to produce material suitable for Deputy Minister and Minister-level audiences. A proven ability to function independently and in a team environment is essential. Awareness of existing GoA and departmental IT policies, procedures, standards, guidelines and practices, and of vendor licensing and procurement constructs, is an asset.

Duties:

Responsible for the coordination and completion of AI enablement projects across licensing and consumption, cloud platform and integration, governance and security, and training and adoption. Oversees all aspects of assigned projects. Sets deadlines, assigns responsibilities, monitors and summarizes progress, and prepares reports for senior management on project status. Builds and maintains working relationships with branch directors, team members, vendors, ministries and other partners.

Project leadership and governance

  • Compile project charters and business/project plans, including the most suitable approach for each project, to ensure business objectives, cost transparency and data integrity are achieved.
  • Collaborate with business and IT leadership to develop a well-defined project plan stating objectives, scope, assumptions, timeline, resource requirements, risks, benefits and budget.
  • Manage multiple concurrent projects for different directors and sponsors, balancing shifting priorities, shared resources and cross-project dependencies, and escalating conflicts to the Executive Director as required.
  • Work with project sponsors and the project management office to develop a project organization structure with clearly defined roles and responsibilities for all stakeholders.
  • Develop project schedule plans and strategies, estimate resource requirements, develop and monitor work plans, and take corrective action for completion of project tasks.
  • Document and report project status against established objectives, milestones, budget and resources, and facilitate tracking and closure of issues and risks.
  • Provide guidance to project resources in establishing work priorities and prompt delivery of project tasks.
  • Work within the standards defined by the project management office and, in the absence of standards, work with the project management office to define new standards.

Enterprise AI licence and consumption enablement

  • Plan and manage the rollout, allocation and lifecycle of enterprise AI licences across ministries. This includes allocation models, quota tracking, bulk provisioning through ServiceNow, licence reassignment and reclamation, and management of demand that exceeds available allocation.
  • Manage the development and implementation of chargeback and cost-recovery mechanisms for AI licences and consumption-based services, in coordination with finance, procurement and ministry stakeholders.
  • Support the onboarding of new providers, models and agents to the approved catalogue, including licensing terms, cost treatment and provisioning requirements.
  • Establish and maintain reporting on licence utilization and consumption/spend, and translate that reporting into recommendations for leadership.

AI cloud platform and integration

  • Plan and manage integration and enablement work across cloud, on-premises and direct-to-provider AI platforms. This includes environment, sandbox and landing zone provisioning, API and service enablement, identity and access configuration, and connector/data-source onboarding.
  • Manage projects that document business requirements and design and deliver AI and cloud solutions that comply with, and contribute to, the Ministry's enterprise architecture, security and privacy requirements.
  • Manage model and platform lifecycle activities, including vendor-driven deprecation and migration events. Coordinate the technical and communication response required to avoid service disruption or unplanned cost increases.
  • Plan the transition of new capabilities into ongoing operations, including support models, monitoring, operating documentation and handoff to operations teams.
  • Coordinate with vendors and delivery partners on deployment schedules, support models, training delivery, and licensing and consumption commitments.

Governance, security, privacy and intake alignment

  • Work through the branch intake and assessment process to confirm each project's scope, value, risk and priority before initiation.
  • Coordinate Security Threat and Risk Assessments (STRAs), Privacy Impact Assessments (PIAs), and information-classification and data-residency reviews. Obtain the approvals required from security, privacy, legal and enterprise architecture partners before a capability is released.
  • Apply the branch's responsible AI standards and guardrails to project design, testing and release, and document how identified risks are addressed.
  • Plan and coordinate User Acceptance Testing and release-readiness reviews to confirm capabilities meet functional, security and privacy requirements.

Training, adoption and change management

  • Coordinate with the Alberta AI Academy to plan role-based training and learning pathways for each rollout, including vendor-supported training.
  • Coordinate with the AI Delivery and Enablement Champion network and ministry leadership to support allocation decisions, adoption planning, use-case identification and escalation of ministry-specific needs.
  • Develop requirements documentation, user-facing guidance, support pathways and knowledge articles required for a capability to be released as a supported service.
  • Provide leadership and assistance to business and project teams that require change management and communication support.
  • Track training completion and adoption against targets, and recommend actions where uptake is below expectations.
  • Capture lessons learned and successful approaches from each rollout so they can be reused across ministries.

Pilots to governed enterprise service

  • Plan and manage pilots of emerging AI capabilities from intake through to a recommendation on enterprise enablement. This includes cohort selection, vendor-supported training, use-case capture, evaluation criteria, and determining cost and governance treatment.

Reporting and stakeholder management

  • Produce and package deliverables for presentation to internal support teams, steering committees, executive and ministerial audiences, and other project stakeholders.
  • Develop recommendations including details of resource requirements, dependencies, interdependencies, policy implications and the methodology to be applied.
  • Work with project sponsors to ensure effective project communication exists for the duration of the project, including escalation of risks as required.
  • Take responsibility for ongoing client satisfaction, including managing peer-level client relationships and overcoming hurdles to ensure win-win solutions.
  • In collaboration with project sponsors, assess whether the project achieved stated outcomes and identify opportunities for improvement for future similar projects.

Mindrift connects specialists with project-based AI opportunities for leading tech companies, focused on testing, evaluating, and improving AI systems. Participation is project-based.

What this opportunity involves

We’re looking for US-based, actively practicing physicians (MD/DO) to evaluate clinical EHR vignettes for a medical AI evaluation program. General and internal medicine are our main focus. While each project involves unique tasks, contributors may:

  • Evaluate clinical EHR vignettes paired with a question, a proposed answer, and a distractor “trap” answer across diagnosis and treatment tasks, spanning cardiovascular, nervous, hematologic, respiratory, digestive, urinary, reproductive, musculoskeletal, and integumentary systems;
  • Score the clinical reasoning quality of benchmark items: vignette accuracy and completeness, whether the vignette gives the answer away, answer correctness and gradeability, and trap quality;
  • Check whether the reasoning chain reaches the answer from vignette facts alone, correct reasoning traces, and write short rationales;
  • Work within three independent blind reads, followed by physician adjudication. Real clinical complexity only. You’re improving the AI tools you’ll eventually use yourself.

If you’re a practicing physician ready to take on this challenging and engaging project, join us!

What we look for

This opportunity is a good fit for US-based physicians open to part-time, non-permanent projects. Ideally, contributors will have:

  • Medical degree (MD or DO) and an active, unrestricted US medical license (verified with the issuing medical board);
  • Board certification or completed residency training, with recent direct patient care (attending-level preferred);
  • Broad, multi-system diagnostic and treatment experience (internal, family, emergency, or hospital medicine);
  • Strong clinical reasoning: differential diagnosis, next-step management, and application of evidence-based guidelines;
  • Prior experience in medical AI evaluation, clinical content or exam-question review, or medical annotation/QA (a plus);
  • Strong written English (C1+).

This opportunity is not fit to medical students, unlicensed medical graduates, non-physician clinicians (NPs, PAs, nurses, pharmacists), or non-clinical healthcare titles.

Project time expectations

For this project, tasks are estimated to require around 10-20 hours per week during active phases, based on project requirements. This is an estimate, not a guaranteed workload, and applies only while the project is active. Tasks must be submitted by the deadline and meet the listed acceptance criteria to be accepted.

Compensation

Paid per accepted task. Your rate depends on the qualification tier you reach and how efficiently you complete tasks — up to the equivalent of $130/hr. Because payment is per approved task, a faster pace raises your effective hourly rate.

About the Role

Abnormal is growing fast, and the way we show up in the world has to keep pace. Our Strategic Events are where our story stops being a pitch and starts being an experience, where CISOs and practitioners walk in curious and walk out convinced. This role will support the strategic events programs across EMEA, including major third-party events, flagship first-party events, and high-profile executive events.

As Strategic Events Specialist, EMEA, you'll bring new ideas and experiences to how we create impact across our events program. You're someone who thrives on a great project plan, keeping deadlines tracked and on target, and managing multiple stakeholders at once across different time zones. Your communication is second to none, and you're always thinking one step ahead when it comes to delivering an event, pre-event and on-site. You understand the importance of an event running smoothly, and love learning as you go to optimise for the future.

This role is perfect for somebody looking for their next step up: a hands-on IC role where you’ll play a lead role in some of our largest flagship events across EMEA, and pitch in on general team tasks day to day. You'll run established event formats independently and apply good judgement within known processes, while leaning on your manager for guidance on new or first-of-their-kind activations. If that sounds like your kind of thing, we want to hear from you!

How You'll Deliver Impact

Project Management, Event Logistics & Vendor Management

  • Support all event logistics end to end and take full ownership of numerous projects, such as creative tasks, room blocks, catering orders, swag orders, staff schedules, promotional assets, and much more.
  • Help coordinate with external stakeholders, such as venues, agencies, event organisers, hotels, couriers, and many more.
  • Help source agencies, venues, production partners and suppliers.
  • Assist with run-of-shows, timelines and contingency plans across multiple concurrent events and markets.
  • Coordinate invitation strategy, registration, attendee communications and internal promotion so the right people show up, market by market.

Regional Strategy & Portfolio Support

  • Support the EMEA strategic event mapping and calendar planning, prioritising investment against pipeline and account-engagement goals.
  • Share experiences and feedback on which events make most sense for our strategic events program across EMEA.

Internal Cross-Functional & Partner/Alliance Collaboration

  • Build relationships with Regional Revenue Marketing, Sales, SDR/BDR, Customer Marketing, Product, Sales Engineering, Partner/Alliance Marketing and Brand/Creative across regions and time zones.
  • Work closely with the Revenue Marketing Manager team to ensure Sales are fully enabled on all event details and what is expected of them.

Budget Ownership & ROI Tracking

  • Support budget tracking for your owned events and the events you support.
  • Suggest alternative, more cost-effective ways of doing things at events, including researching vendors and agencies for cost comparisons.
  • Budget admin, including raising purchase orders, submitting invoices, and updating budget management tools.

On-Site Execution

  • Lead on-site at your own events, including training other on-site team members and coordinating and leading staff orientations.
  • Support on-site execution for flagship regional events, directing any temporary or contract event staff and troubleshooting in real time.
  • Set clear expectations on-site for all teams by hosting staff orientations virtually and in person

Post-Event Follow-Up & Program Result Accountability

  • Post-event admin, including list uploads and sending post-event reports.
  • Help build repeatable regional playbooks and share best practice with peers across the broader Strategic Events team, including other regions
  • Run post-event retrospectives and apply lessons learned to improve the next event, raising the bar for the regional program as it scales
  • Ensure tight alignment with regional teams to ensure full ROI of event is realised, by sharing regular lead status update reports

What You Bring

  • 2–4 years' experience in B2B events or experiential marketing, ideally within technology, SaaS, cybersecurity or enterprise software.
  • Experience of owning established, repeatable event formats end-to-end — not just coordinating logistics for someone else's plan — with sound judgement on known procedures and a willingness to ask for guidance on new or first-of-their-kind activations.
  • Experience running executive-level programmes (dinners, roundtables, advisory boards) as well as larger conference/trade show activations.
  • Multi-market EMEA experience and the ability to work across different time zones and regions.
  • Strong program management habits: organised, deadline-driven, and increasingly independent on routine work.
  • Budget, vendor and contract management experience across multiple concurrent workstreams.
  • Confidence working cross-functionally with Sales, SDR/BDR and Marketing stakeholders, and translating event activity into commercial outcomes.
  • Comfortable presenting event results and ROI to stakeholders using registration, pipeline and engagement data.
  • Willingness to travel roughly 40–50%, mainly across EMEA, with some APAC and AMER travel, including evening/weekend work around live events.

Cybersecurity or enterprise software experience is a plus, not a requirement. What matters is commercial judgement, regional ownership, and exceptional execution.

Preferred

  • Experience with event and marketing technology such as Asana, Allocadia, Coupa, Jifflenow, Cvent, Salesforce, Sigma, Splash, RainFocus, Claude, and Google Suite.
  • An additional European language.
  • Familiarity with account-based marketing (ABM) principles and target-account event strategies.

The Ideal Candidate

You know a great event is not a logistics exercise. It's a story told in three dimensions — one that brings a brand to life, earns trust with prospects and customers, arms the sales team, and produces measurable business impact.

You're equally at home building a project plan in a spreadsheet and troubleshooting a badge-printer jam at 7am. You're calm when things go sideways, direct when something isn't working, and generous with your stakeholders when it goes right.

Most of all, you care about the craft. The details other people don't notice are exactly the ones you fix.

What Success Looks Like

  • Your events are delivered flawlessly and consistently
  • Registrations, attendance, meetings and pipeline consistently hit or beat plan for the events you own.
  • Budgets and vendor relationships are managed with discipline and transparency.
  • Every event has a clear measurement story and a defensible ROI.

At Talkspace, we are committed to fostering a diverse, equitable, inclusive, and belonging-centered workplace where everyone can thrive while making a difference in mental health. Want to help over two million people receive quality mental healthcare? Come join our mission to get therapy into the hands of everyone!

We’re looking for a part-time, contract Therapist (Independent Contract Provider) who is passionate about reaching individuals who need mental healthcare but lack easy access to it. This role is perfect for those seeking the opportunity to work with a diverse client base while enjoying the flexibility and rewards of private practice—without the hassle of administrative work. Let Talkspace handle the insurance billing, marketing, and administrative costs, so you can create your own schedule and focus fully on providing impactful care!

What you'll do:

  • Treat clients remotely in your state(s) of licensure on the secure (HIPAA compliant) Talkspace platform
  • Conduct client sessions using video, audio, and live messaging services
  • Respond to asynchronous client messages each week, in a timely manner
  • Complete your required clinical documentation after each client session

About you

  • Current license to practice independently without supervision in the state of Wisconsin
    • Licensed Clinical Social Worker (LCSW)
    • Licensed Marriage and Family Therapist (LMFT)
    • Licensed Professional Counselor (LPC)
  • Individual professional malpractice liability insurance policy
  • Individual NPI number
  • Comfortable learning new online tools and technology
  • Reliable internet connection and video-capable device

Perks

  • Clients Ready for You: Talkspace provides new client referrals
  • Flexible Schedule: Set your own schedule with no minimum requirement for your weekly hours or caseload size
  • No Membership Fees: No provider fees
  • Accept Insurance Without Hassle: Talkspace will take care of all aspects of client insurance including credentialing, billing, and claims
  • Everything in One Place: Sessions, clinical documentation, resources, and compensation tracking on one platform
  • Fully Paid Training: Master the Talkspace platform before your first session
  • Clinical Support: Provider Support and IT teams available for any technical or platform related questions
  • Free CEUs: NBCC and ASWB accredited continuing education credits via Talkspace-provided Learning Communities
  • Health Perks: Access Stride Health to support your health and financial well-being

Compensation

  • $70 per hour for live chat, audio, or video sessions (this rate is prorated for 45 and 30 minute sessions)
  • Additional compensation for asynchronous messaging
  • Earn a new client engagement bonus, varying by plan type

Please note: If you treat clients in multiple states, different rates will apply accordingly. Rates could be subject to change and may vary over time based on the market and shifts in demand.

Why Talkspace

Talkspace is a leading virtual behavioral healthcare provider committed to helping people lead healthier, happier lives through access to high-quality mental healthcare. At Talkspace, we believe that mental healthcare is core to overall health and should be available to everyone.

Talkspace pioneered the ability to text with a licensed therapist from anywhere and now offers a comprehensive suite of mental health services, including therapy for individuals, teens, and couples, as well as psychiatric treatment and medication management (18+). With Talkspace’s core therapy offerings, members are matched with one of thousands of licensed therapists within days and can engage in live video, audio, or chat sessions, and/or unlimited asynchronous text messaging sessions.

All care offered at Talkspace is delivered through an easy-to-use, fully-encrypted web and mobile platform that meets HIPAA, federal, and state regulatory requirements. More than 151 million Americans have access to Talkspace through their health insurance plans, employee assistance programs, our partnerships with leading healthcare companies, or as a free benefit through their employer, school, or government agency.

EQUAL OPPORTUNITY EMPLOYER

Talkspace welcomes and celebrates talent from all backgrounds, perspectives, and walks of life to foster an innovative and diverse workforce. We encourage you to apply, even if you don’t meet every qualification or if your path has been nontraditional — such as not completing a formal degree program, taking a career break, or having a prior criminal record — if you believe you could make a great addition to this team. Come as you are and learn about the exciting opportunities on our team.

Individuals seeking employment at Talkspace are considered without regard to race, color, religious creed, sex, national origin, citizenship status, age, physical or mental disability, sexual orientation, marital, parental, veteran or military status, unfavorable military discharge, or any other status protected by applicable federal, state or local law.

How do we define Diversity, Equity, Inclusion, and Belonging at Talkspace?

Diversity

Diversity encompasses the unique attributes of our employees as individuals. We value and embrace the richness arising from their varied backgrounds, perspectives, and experiences, which include, but are not limited to, age, ability, ethnicity, gender, race, and cultural background.

Equity

Equity refers to a fair and impartial workplace, aiming to ensure equal growth and advancement opportunities for all employees. This involves amplifying underrepresented voices, addressing unconscious biases, and providing inclusive, culturally competent mental health care.

Inclusion

Inclusion signifies the practice of granting equal access to opportunities and resources for all employees, particularly those who might otherwise be excluded or marginalized. It ensures that everyone feels a sense of belonging, value, support, and respect as an individual.

Belonging

Belonging reflects the affinity and positive relationships that develop among employees from diverse backgrounds when businesses actively promote diversity, equity, and inclusion in the workplace.

jobs.excerpt: We are seeking a Senior Solutions Architect with deep security expertise to join the Voyager team in the Mirantis Office of the CTO.
jobs.description:
We are seeking a Senior Solutions Architect with deep security expertise to join the Voyager team in the Mirantis Office of the CTO. You will own the security solutioning of k0rdent AI, our platform for building and operating GPU clouds and AI factories, from metal to model.

You will define how k0rdent AI environments are secured end to end: the hardware and firmware they boot from, the hosts, virtual machines and Kubernetes clusters they run, the networks and storage they share, the secrets and certificates that hold them together, and the AI models and applications they serve. You will turn that design into published reference architectures, working code and proofs of concept that run on real hardware with our customers and partners.

As part of the Office of the CTO, research is a core part of the job. You will explore threats, designs and technologies before customers ask for them, prototype ideas that may not ship, and challenge established practice when a better approach exists. Your work will shape where k0rdent AI goes next, not only how it is deployed today.

This role combines research with hands-on, outward-facing work. You will split your time between exploring new designs, writing architecture, building and validating it in the lab, and explaining it to engineers, security teams, executives and conference audiences. You will work with Solutions Architects, Partner Management and Engineering colleagues across many countries and time zones.

Key Responsibilities

Reference architecture

  • Design and publish security reference architectures and solution designs for k0rdent AI, covering single-tenant private AI clouds, multi-tenant GPU clouds and hybrid deployments that span public cloud and on-premises infrastructure.

  • Define a defence-in-depth model across the stack, from hardware root of trust and firmware to hosts, virtual machines, Kubernetes, networks, storage, models and applications.

  • Define tenant isolation boundaries and their guarantees, and document where each boundary is strong, where it is weak, and what it costs to strengthen.

  • Map designs to the controls and frameworks customers must meet, and document trade-offs (risk, cost, performance, operability) with defensible reasoning a customer can follow.

Platform and infrastructure security

  • Bare-metal and host security: secure and measured boot, TPM-based attestation, BMC and Redfish hardening, firmware integrity, and hardened Linux hosts.

  • Virtual machine security: hypervisor and KubeVirt hardening, VM isolation, and the security implications of PCI passthrough and SR-IOV for GPUs and NICs.

  • Kubernetes security: RBAC, Pod Security Standards, admission control and policy-as-code, runtime security, and secure multi-cluster and multi-tenant operation.

  • Secrets management: secret stores, KMS and HSM integration, envelope encryption, secret delivery to workloads, and rotation.

  • Certificates and PKI: internal certificate authorities, automated issuance and rotation, mTLS between services, and workload identity.

  • Network security: segmentation and zero-trust designs, Kubernetes network policy, tenant isolation on front-end and GPU fabrics, and DPU-based security enforcement.

  • Storage security: encryption at rest and in transit, key management, and tenant isolation on shared block, file and object storage used for training data and model weights.

  • Public cloud security: secure landing zones, identity and access management, and network controls on major public clouds, and how they extend to hybrid deployments.

AI model and application security

  • Define how Transformer-based models are protected through their lifecycle: provenance and signing of model weights, integrity of training and fine-tuning data, and secure model registries.

  • Secure inference services and AI applications against threats such as prompt injection, data and model exfiltration, model theft and abuse of agentic tool access.

  • Design isolation for shared GPU infrastructure (MIG, vGPU, passthrough) and assess confidential computing options for protecting models and data in use.

  • Secure the software supply chain for platforms, containers and models: image signing, SBOMs, vulnerability management and provenance.

Research and exploration

  • Track and evaluate emerging security technologies, standards and threats, such as confidential computing on GPUs, remote attestation, post-quantum cryptography, model signing and AI agent security.

  • Prototype alternative designs in the lab, including ones customers have not yet asked for, and measure them against current practice.

  • Challenge established or customer-preferred designs when evidence points to a better option, and make the case with data.

  • Publish findings as internal research notes and design proposals and, where appropriate, as external papers, blog posts or talks.

Code and proofs of concept

  • Build and run proofs of concept with customers and partners, on Mirantis lab hardware and on customer sites, and report results against agreed success criteria.

  • Write automation, policies and tooling (Python, Go, Bash, Ansible, Helm, Kubernetes manifests, Terraform, policy-as-code) that make the reference architectures reproducible.

  • Assess designs and deployments through threat modelling, configuration review and hands-on testing, and turn findings into design guidance.

Customers, partners and community

  • Act as the security subject matter expert in customer discovery, design reviews and architecture workshops, bringing thought leadership and new ideas rather than only reflecting current practice.

  • Engage with customer security, risk and compliance teams, and support security questionnaires and architecture reviews for strategic opportunities.

  • Work with hardware, software and security partners (e.g. NVIDIA, server OEMs, security vendors) on joint designs and validations.

  • Innovate and feed research results back to Product, Engineering and the Mirantis security team, and help shape the k0rdent AI roadmap.

  • Present at industry events, webinars and partner summits, and run hands-on workshops for technical audiences.

  • Write technical content: reference architecture documents, solution briefs, blog posts and internal enablement.

Location, travel and working model

This role is remote and based in the United States, with a strong preference for the East Coast.

  • You will work with a team spread across many time zones; some meetings will fall outside standard local hours.

  • Travel of up to 25% for customer engagements, partner meetings, lab work and industry events, primarily within the US and EU.

  • Mirantis is an equal opportunity employer. Compensation and benefits are set according to the local market and employment arrangement.

Education and experience

  • Bachelor's degree in Computer Science, Computer Engineering, Cybersecurity or a related field, or equivalent practical experience.

  • 8+ years in security engineering or security architecture, with at least 3 years securing cloud, Kubernetes or large-scale infrastructure platforms.

  • Customer-facing experience as a solutions architect, pre-sales engineer, consultant or technical lead.

Required technical skills

  • Cloud security: designing and operating secure deployments on at least one major public cloud (AWS, Azure or GCP) and on private cloud or bare-metal infrastructure.

  • Host and virtualisation security: Linux hardening (e.g. SELinux or AppArmor, CIS benchmarks), secure boot, TPM, and hypervisor and VM isolation, including KubeVirt.

  • Kubernetes security: RBAC, Pod Security Standards, admission controllers and policy engines (e.g. Kyverno, OPA Gatekeeper), runtime security (e.g. Falco), and multi-tenancy patterns.

  • Secrets and key management: tools such as HashiCorp Vault or OpenBao, External Secrets Operator, cloud KMS and HSMs.

  • PKI and identity: certificate lifecycle with tools such as cert-manager, mTLS, OIDC and SSO, and workload identity (e.g. SPIFFE/SPIRE).

  • Network security: segmentation, firewalling, zero-trust architectures and Kubernetes network policy (e.g. Cilium, Calico).

  • Storage and data security: encryption at rest and in transit, key hierarchy design, and access control on shared storage.

  • AI security: a working understanding of how Transformer-based models are trained, packaged and served, and the threats specific to them (e.g. OWASP Top 10 for LLM Applications, MITRE ATLAS).

  • Software supply chain security: image signing (e.g. Sigstore/cosign), SBOMs, vulnerability scanning and SLSA concepts.

  • Programming or scripting in at least one language (Python or Go preferred), and comfortable using Git, CI and infrastructure-as-code.

How you work

We hire for these behaviours as much as for technical depth, and will ask for concrete examples of each.

  • Curious. You dig into how attacks actually work, read the specs, advisories and source, and keep up with how AI and infrastructure threats are changing. You question established designs, including the ones customers are used to, when there is a better way.

  • Ownership. You take a reference architecture or a POC from the first sketch to a published, validated result, and you stand behind it.

  • Proactive. You spot risks and gaps in the product, the documentation or a customer design before you are asked, and you act on them.

  • Fast learner. You get productive quickly in unfamiliar hardware, software or customer environments.

  • Business acumen. You frame security decisions in terms of risk, cost, compliance and time-to-value, and explain them in those terms to decision makers.

Communication and collaboration

  • Excellent written and spoken English; you write documents others can build from.

  • Comfortable presenting to large audiences at conferences and events, and running hands-on workshops.

  • Able to adapt the message to the audience, from engineers to CISOs and customer executives.

  • Experience working in an international, distributed company, across time zones and different work cultures, with Solutions Architects, Partner Management and Engineering teams.

Nice to have

  • Experience with compliance frameworks and benchmarks relevant to cloud and AI infrastructure, such as NIST SP 800-53, NIST AI RMF, FedRAMP, SOC 2, ISO/IEC 27001, CIS benchmarks or DISA STIGs.

  • Hands-on experience with confidential computing (e.g. AMD SEV-SNP, Intel TDX, NVIDIA GPU confidential computing) and remote attestation.

  • Experience securing GPU cloud, neocloud or HPC environments, or NVIDIA Cloud Partner (NCP) style deployments.

  • Experience with DPUs (e.g. NVIDIA BlueField) for infrastructure isolation and security offload.

  • Offensive security or red-teaming experience, including against AI systems.

  • Experience with Mirantis products, MKE, k0s, k0rdent security.

  • Security certifications such as CISSP, CCSP, CKS, OSCP, or public cloud security specialty certifications.

  • Contributions to open-source security or Kubernetes projects, or a track record of public talks and technical writing.

  • Participation in standards or industry bodies (e.g. CNCF TAG Security, OpenSSF, Confidential Computing Consortium, CoSAI), or published research, CVEs, patents or white papers.

  • Additional languages beyond English.

Why you’ll love Mirantis

  • Build the observability foundation for the AI cloud era, working directly with leading GPU cloud operators, NeoClouds, sovereign clouds, and AI-first enterprises

  • Collaborate with a world-class, distributed team committed to openness and technical excellence

  • Shape the product narrative and influence go-to-market success

jobs.description:
Please note that we are unable to consider applications from candidates based in France, Italy, or Germany for this role.

Money is moving onto the internet, and the shift has a name: Open Money. This is money that is open, portable, agentic, and owned by you. MetaMask spent the last ten years building it; with 100M+ downloads, users in ~190 countries, and trillions in cumulative transaction volume, it's the most trusted self-custodial financial platform on the internet. Now we're building the operating system for your money: one place to hold, move, grow, and use anything you own. Join a remote-first, global team rebuilding how money works: a problem that touches everyone, every day.

About MetaMask

MetaMask is building a future where users can unlock the full product stack through a single, seamless identity experience, enabling access to all features with trust, safety, and minimal friction.

Today, identity verification is fragmented across several product and onboarding experiences. Users are repeatedly asked to verify themselves across different services, creating unnecessary friction, inconsistent outcomes, and degraded trust.

Universal KYC (UKYC) is a new initiative to solve this problem by creating a single, reusable identity layer across MetaMask. At the centre of this is MetaMask Passport, a product designed to enable users to verify once and unlock multiple experiences across the MetaMask ecosystem.

This role sits at the intersection of platform and product experience. You will define the primitives, standards, and user journeys that make identity verification seamless, privacy-conscious, and globally compliant.

What you’ll do

You will own the vision and roadmap for Universal KYC and MetaMask Passport, defining how a reusable identity layer unlocks the broader MetaMask product stack. You will build the underlying identity platform, creating scalable verification primitives and standards that can be adopted across products. In parallel, you will design a seamless, low-friction KYC experience that reduces time-to-first-transaction while maintaining compliance integrity. You will drive adoption across MetaMask by partnering closely with internal teams to integrate a consistent identity layer, while balancing privacy, trust, and global regulatory requirements. Throughout, you will lead execution end-to-end, aligning cross-functional teams and delivering measurable outcomes.

What we are looking for:

  • Proven experience building or scaling identity verification (IDV), KYC, or onboarding products
  • Strong background in fintech, ideally with exposure to Web3
  • Hands-on experience working with identity verification providers (IDV vendors) such as Sumsub, Veriff, Onfido, Persona, or Stripe Identity
  • Familiarity with compliance workflows, including KYC, KYB, and customer due diligence (CDD) processes
  • Track record of delivering platform products adopted across multiple teams
  • Ability to operate across both technical systems and user experience

What Success looks like:

  • Increased KYC completion rates and reduced onboarding friction
  • Reduced time-to-first-transaction across KYC-gated flows
  • Increased reuse of verified identity across products
  • Improved transaction success rate through consistent verification outcomes
  • Strong user trust with minimal friction and compliant execution

Attributes that will make you stand out

  • First-principles thinker with strong product judgment
  • Deep user empathy with a focus on reducing friction and cognitive load
  • Strong understanding of trust, privacy, and compliance trade-offs
  • Clear, structured communicator who drives alignment and momentum
  • High ownership and ability to operate in ambiguity

Why This Role Matters

Universal KYC is a foundational unlock for MetaMask, enabling users to move from fragmented, repetitive identity verification to a seamless, reusable experience across the entire product stack. It establishes a scalable, privacy-conscious identity layer that strengthens user trust while meeting global compliance requirements.
